title: Automate mapping of postmortem actions to verifiable PRD requirements and test contracts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reproducible pipeline and PRD template that converts validated postmortem action items into scoped product requirements with attached acceptance tests, telemetry contracts, and owner assignments. The goal is to shorten the time between incident postmortem and verifiable PRD updates so engineering can implement mitigations with clear success criteria and observability requirements.
background: Recent incidents around KV cache regeneration and cold-start autoscaling have produced high-quality postmortem action lists, but it often takes multiple cycles and manual coordination to translate those actions into PRD-ready requirements. This gap causes delays in rollouts and inconsistent acceptance criteria across teams, increasing risk of recurrence and obscuring verification. Engineering and SRE have requested a more deterministic handoff that includes testable telemetry and rollout gates.
goals: Define a small, extensible PRD template that embeds incident action items as discrete requirements
Automate mapping from postmortem action items (Confluence/Drive) to draft PRD entries with proposed owners and test types
Require telemetry contract snippets and SLO/alert updates to be attached to each requirement
Enable product owners and engineers to accept/modify suggested scope with a single review workflow
Ship a set of acceptance-test harness templates (synthetic, integration, and canary checks) to verify mitigations before rollback-free rollout
scope_changes: This expands the scope of the existing postmortem-to-action process by adding an automated draft PRD generator and test-harness templates. It does NOT include building the full CI gating for rollout enforcement in this ticket; that is scoped to a follow-up engineering epic (ENG-43011).
requirements: PRD template fields: incident reference, rationale, proposed requirement, owner, estimate, telemetry contract, SLO delta, acceptance tests, rollout gate
Mapping script that ingests postmortem action items (structured text or bullet list) and creates draft PRD entries in the internal PRD tracker
UI flow for product owners to accept, edit, or reject generated entries and to assign engineering owners
Telemetry contract format: metric name, expected delta, query example, dashboard link, alert rule GUID placeholder
Acceptance test templates: synthetic latency/throughput test, deterministic regression check, canary traffic validation recipe
Linking mechanism to attach generated PRD entries to issue keys (ENG-/DES- prefixes) and to create follow-up Linear tickets when accepted
Minimum artifact list required to mark a requirement as 'Ready for Implementation' (owner, estimate, telemetry snippet, acceptance test plan)
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed incident postmortem in Confluence, when the mapping script runs, then it produces a draft PRD file with at least one requirement and suggested owner or assignment pool
Each generated requirement includes a telemetry contract snippet and at least one suggested acceptance test type
Product owner can accept and convert a draft requirement into a live PRD section with one confirmation action in the PRD editor UI
Accepted requirement automatically creates a Linked Linear ticket with correct team prefix and copies the acceptance-test template into the ticket description
There is a sample runbook that demonstrates how to validate the acceptance tests end-to-end against a synthetic workload in the staging cluster
A smoke verification (manual) demonstrates that the new process reduces postmortem-to-PRD lead time by >= 50% in the pilot (measured on three incidents)
success_metrics: Lead time from postmortem publication to PRD-ready requirements (target: <= 3 business days)
Percentage of postmortem actions converted to PRD requirements without manual rework (target: >= 70% for pilot incidents)
Number of production regressions attributable to the same failure class within 90 days (target: decrease by 30%)
Adoption: at least two product teams use the generator in the first 6 weeks
rollout_plan: Pilot with serving-infra and SRE for 3 incidents: run mapping script, gather feedback, refine telemetry contract format, then enable generator for all incidents in the reliability namespace. Phase 2 will integrate with CI gating and automatic ticket creation for accepted requirements (ENG-43011).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Generated requirements are low quality and require heavy manual edits — Mitigation: Start with conservative parsing and require PO sign-off; include a feedback loop to improve NLP mappings
Risk: Telemetry contracts are inconsistent across teams — Mitigation: Provide canonical metric examples and enforce metric validation in review checklist
Risk: Owners are mis-assigned by the script — Mitigation: Suggest ownership pools instead of single owners where confidence is low
Risk: Security-sensitive incidents leak details into draft PRDs — Mitigation: Mask PII/secret snippets in the automated draft and require manual review for sensitive incidents
